2.

The instant interlocutory application has been filed under section 430(1) of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (in short 'BNSS') for consideration of the appellant's prayer for suspension of his sentence and release on bail during the pendency of the appeal.

3. This appeal has been preferred against the judgment of conviction dated 31.01.2023 and order of sentence dated 02.02.2023 passed by the court of learned Additional District & Sessions Judge-XIII,
Saran at Chapra, in Sessions Trial Case No. 344 of 2019 arising out of Baniyapur P.S. Case No. 110 of 2019, whereby and whereunder the appellant has been convicted for the Patna High Court CR.

. 
4. Mr. Rajesh Roy, learned counsel appearing for the appellant submits that the major punishment awarded upon the appellant is 10 years of rigorous imprisonment for the offences under each sections 489A and 489B of the IPC and this is the second attempt of the appellant to get the same relief and his earlier prayer was rejected vide order dated 01.04.2024 giving the appellant a liberty to renew his bail prayer after one year from the date of that order on this condition, if his appeal is Chandan Kumar Singh vs The State Of Bihar on 8 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/72217961/
1 not taken up for hearing in the said period of one year.

sentences.text: It is further submitted that the instant appeal relates to the year 2023 and presently, it is not listed before any bench and the appellant has served about 6 years and 5 months in jail till date and in the present scenario of the hearing of the criminal appeals by the Cr. APP(SJ) Benches, there is less possibility of early hearing of the appellant's appeal and the fresh ground for renewing the prayer is only the appellant's long incarceration period in jail as well as unlikelihood of his appeal to be taken up for hearing in near future.
5. On the other hand, Mr. Syed Ashfaque Ahmad, learned APP for the State submits that while opposing the first prayer of the appellant, State has filed the written objection on Patna High Court CR.

APP (SJ) No.2390 of 2023(8) dt.08-08-2025 merit of the allegation and the same may be treated as written objection to the present prayer though the appellant has not prayed for the relief under section 430(1) of BNSS, on the merit of the allegation.
It is further submitted that there is serious allegation against the appellant relating to large number of counterfeit currency notes being found in his possession, for which he has been convicted.
6. Heard both the sides and perused the relevant materials.

Though against this appellant, there is serious allegation, however, considering his present custody period which has been about 6 years and 5 months against the major punishment of 10 years of rigorous imprisonment and in view of aforesaid scenario of the hearing of the criminal appeals by the Cr. APP(SJ) Benches, in which the appellants are in jail, there is less possibility of hearing of this appeal in near future, so keeping in view this aspect, this Court is now inclined to grant the relief under section 430(1) of the BNSS to the appellant.

Accordingly, let the appellant named above be enlarged on bail during the pendency of this appeal on furnishing bail bond of Rs. 20,000/- (Rupees Twenty Thousand) with two sureties of the like amount each to the satisfaction of the learned Additional District & Sessions Judge- XIII,
Saran at Chapra, in Sessions Trial Case No. 344 of 2019 arising out of Baniyapur P.S. Case No. 110 of 2019.
